title: Integral quasi-coherent algebras on qcqs spaces admit finite finitely presented directed approximations
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and suppose $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Here quasi-compact means every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover, using [def-a1-space-point-topology], and quasi-separated means the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests. Let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ whose underlying module is quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Suppose it is integral: for every affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, every element of $\mathcal A(U)$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $R$. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$, quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\mathcal A_i$, algebra maps $\alpha_{ji}:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A_j$ for $i\le j$ satisfying the identity and composition laws, and compatible algebra maps $\alpha_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$, such that every $\mathcal A_i$ is finite and finitely presented as an algebra. Explicitly, for each affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, $\mathcal A_i(U)$ is a finite $R$-module and has a presentation $R[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ with finite $n,m$. The cocone $(\mathcal A,(\alpha_i))$ is a colimit in the category of quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras: compatible maps $\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal B$ to any such algebra $\mathcal B$ factor uniquely through an algebra map $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Neither the transition maps nor the maps to $\mathcal A$ are required to be injective.

source.place: Tag 082C (lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite), clause (2); its algebra conventions are tested on affine etale schemes. The chart/topological quasi-compactness equivalence is Tag 03E4 (spaces-properties.tex, lemma-quasi-compact-space).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-fp-directed-approximation] to the underlying module of $\mathcal A$. Reindex its small filtered diagram by the directed-cofinal theorem [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to obtain $\mathcal A=\varinjlim_I\mathcal F_i$ with finitely presented terms and linear transitions $f_{ji}$. Put $\mathcal S_i=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F_i)$, and let $\psi_i:\mathcal S_i\to\mathcal A$ extend the cocone map. The symmetric-algebra universal property gives transitions $\sigma_{ji}=\operatorname{Sym}(f_{ji})$, with identity, composition and $\psi_j\sigma_{ji}=\psi_i$.

Let $\mathcal J_i=\ker\psi_i$ and $\mathcal B_i=\operatorname{Im}\psi_i=\mathcal S_i/\mathcal J_i$, using [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. These are quasi-coherent; $\sigma_{ji}(\mathcal J_i)\subseteq\mathcal J_j$ and $\mathcal B_i\subseteq\mathcal B_j$. On each affine etale $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\mathcal F_i(U)$ has finitely many generators. Their symmetric images generate $\mathcal S_i(U)$ as an algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation]; their images in $\mathcal B_i(U)\subseteq\mathcal A(U)$ are integral by the hypothesis. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] makes $\mathcal B_i(U)$ finite over $R$.

source.place: Tag 082C, proof (2), finiteness of the image algebras.

proof.text: The cocone $\mathcal B_i\to\mathcal A$ is colimiting. Indeed on each affine etale $U$, chart evaluation and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] show that every section of $\mathcal A(U)$ comes from some $\mathcal F_i(U)$, hence from $\mathcal B_i(U)$. Equal representatives in two images are equal in a common later image, because its inclusion in $\mathcal A(U)$ is injective. Therefore the directed union is exactly $\mathcal A(U)$, with its algebra operations; [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] gives the algebra-sheaf colimit.

source.place: Tag 082C, last displayed equality, second equality.

proof.text: For each $i$ use [lem-sfb-space-module-fp-directed-approximation] and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to choose $\mathcal J_i=\varinjlim_{K_i}\mathcal E_{ik}$ with finitely presented terms. Put $\mathcal L_{ik}=(\mathcal E_{ik}\to\mathcal J_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal S_i)$ and $\mathcal Q_{ik}=\mathcal S_i/\mathcal L_{ik}$ using [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus]. The charts identify these with ordinary generated ideals and quotients. Since $\mathcal F_i(U)$ is finitely presented and $\mathcal E_{ik}(U)$ finitely generated, [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation] makes each $\mathcal Q_{ik}(U)$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra.

source.place: Tags 082C and 082A, symmetric quotients by finitely generated relations.

proof.text: Order the small set $P=\{(i,k):k\in K_i\}$ by $i\le j$ and $\sigma_{ji}(\mathcal L_{ik})\subseteq\mathcal L_{jl}$. This is a preorder by functoriality of $\sigma$. Given $i\le j$ and $k$, the map $\mathcal E_{ik}\to\mathcal J_i\to\mathcal J_j$ factors through some $\mathcal E_{jl}$ by [lem-sfb-space-fp-module-hom-colimit]; this gives $(i,k)\preceq(j,l)$. To bound two pairs choose a common upper $j$ in $I$, factor both maps there, and take a common upper bound in $K_j$. Thus $P$ is nonempty directed; projection to $I$ is monotone and each $K_i\to P$ is monotone. The induced quotient arrows are unique with $\alpha_{qp}q_p=q_q\sigma_{ji}$, so obey identity and composition.

source.place: Tag 082C, commuting square of relation modules and induced quotient arrow.

proof.text: For fixed $i$, the maps $\mathcal Q_{ik}\to\mathcal B_i$ are colimiting: on an affine etale $U$, every $x\in\mathcal J_i(U)$ is the image of an element of some $\mathcal E_{ik}(U)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise]. Hence $\bigcup_k\mathcal L_{ik}(U)=\mathcal J_i(U)$. A compatible family of algebra maps out of the quotients is exactly an algebra map out of $\mathcal S_i(U)$ killing this union; it factors uniquely through $\mathcal S_i(U)/\mathcal J_i(U)$. The chart criterion [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] gives the row colimit. The row maps satisfy the compatibility equation with every pair arrow, since both composites from $\mathcal S_i$ are its given map to $\mathcal B_j$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-directed-pairs-colimit-transitivity] and step 3 give $\varinjlim_P\mathcal Q_{ik}=\mathcal A$.

source.place: Tag 082C, final displayed equality, first equality and its compatibility.

proof.text: Fix $i$. Choose an affine surjective etale chart $U\to X$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] and finite generators $s_1,\ldots,s_m$ of $\mathcal S_i(U)$ furnished by [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation]. Their images in $\mathcal B_i(U)\subseteq\mathcal A(U)$ satisfy monic polynomials $P_r\in\mathcal O_X(U)[T]$. The chart row-colimit calculation of step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-rings-zero] make each $P_r(s_r)$ vanish in $\mathcal Q_{ik}(U)$ for sufficiently large $k$. Choose one bound $k_0(i)$ for the finite list. At every $k\ge k_0(i)$ the images of the $s_r$ still generate the quotient algebra and are integral; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] makes this quotient a finite module. The finite-type module criterion of [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] descends that property from $U$ and tests it on all affine etale charts. Thus $\mathcal Q_{ik}$ is finite for all $k\ge k_0(i)$.

source.place: Tag 086Z, final paragraph, used in Tag 082C to prove eventual finiteness.

proof.text: Let $P_f=\{(i,k):k\ge k_0(i)\}$. Every pair is below one in $P_f$ by increasing its second coordinate. Two members have a common upper in $P$ and then in $P_f$ by the same operation, so $P_f$ is nonempty directed. Restricting a colimit to this cofinal full subpreorder preserves it by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory](1), applied to the opposite preorders. We have obtained finite finitely presented terms with the inherited maps to $\mathcal A$. Finally apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to $P_f$ if a directed poset rather than a preorder is desired. Its reindexed cocone is the required one. On the empty space the affine chart is $\operatorname{Spec}0$ and there are no nonzero generators or relations to kill.

source.place: Tag 082C, last paragraph; cofinal restriction to the finite stages.
